patch.value:
## Summary

Agents and extensions often read an item, decide something from it (which PR delivered it, whether its acceptance criteria are met, which checkpoint to resume), and then write. Neither the SDK nor the CLI can apply that write only if the item is still the revision the decision was based on. `update`, `close`, `comments --add` and their SDK equivalents take no expected item hash or revision. A concurrent edit between the read and the write is silently built on, so the agent records a decision about state that no longer exists.

The lock-TTL fencing from #1549 makes a single mutation safe. It doesn't cover the gap between an agent's read and its later write.

## Evidence (fleet packages, 2026-10-24, pm 2026.10.20–2026.10.24)

Read-only reviews blocked three separate packages on this class in one day, each reproduced against the real SDK:

- **pm-github closeout:** the delivering PR is chosen from the item's `delivery-pr` tag. If the tag changes from PR #1 to PR #2 while evidence is being fetched, the item still closes with PR #1's provenance. The workaround is a scoped `beforeMutation` hash guard under the item lock plus one retry. The API the agent asked for: `close(id, reason, { expectedItemHash })`.
- **pm-rlm:** failure cleanup read a checkpoint, then saved that stale copy over a concurrent resume's answer, steps and token charges.
- **pm-slack:** outbox retry cleanup deleted a peer drainer's newer group mappings.

Each package had to hand-roll its own guard.

## Reproduction (plain directory, no git)

1. Agent A: `pm get <id> --json`, records `item_hash` H1, decides to close based on the tags it read.
2. Agent B: `pm update <id> --tags delivery-pr:2`, so the hash is now H2.
3. Agent A: `pm close <id> "Delivered by PR 1"` succeeds. There is no way to say "only if the hash is still H1".

## Expected

An optional precondition on every mutating command and SDK method, for example `--expect-hash <item_hash>` / `{ expectedItemHash }`, checked under the item lock as part of the write. On mismatch the write is refused with a typed code (for example `stale_precondition`, exit 2). The refusal returns the current hash, plus a compact summary of which fields changed since H1, so the agent can re-decide in one call. The same option belongs on `update`, `close`, `claim`, `comments/notes/learnings --add`, `files/docs/test --add` and bulk mutations (one hash per id).

## Why core

Read-decide-write is the normal agent loop on a shared tracker. Without a native precondition, every package re-implements a lock-plus-hash check, and the races above ship until a reviewer finds them. This is part of making many agents on one tracker safe without git (#1516 measured the throughput side of the same workload).
GH-1576: guard SDK and CLI mutations with expected item revisions

Reported read-decide-write races in extension consumers need an optional atomic expected-item-hash precondition checked at the mutation commit boundary. Preserve existing no-precondition behavior and distinguish this from mutation lease fencing.

Define a public optional expected revision/hash contract across single-item and bulk SDK/CLI/MCP mutations; Check each precondition under the authoritative item lock at commit time and refuse stale writes without acknowledged item or history changes; Return typed current revision and bounded actionable change evidence; Deterministic concurrent controls cover closeout tags, collection cleanup, claim and bulk partial outcomes without weakening lease fencing.
A write based on a stale observed revision refuses atomically and supplies bounded recovery evidence.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Additional consumer report: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1620 (2026-10-28). Its proposed option 2 is the existing expected-revision acceptance here, so reuse this canonical feature instead of creating duplicate work. Reporter describes a separate-process ordinary SDK writer entering between a transaction inspect and apply, losing title/parent/relation/assignee changes. Current source uses WORKSPACE_TRANSACTION_LOCK_ID for the coordinator while item writes take their own lock; the report is consistent with those distinct scopes, but this intake has not independently executed its probe. Include precise transaction-isolation documentation and a native concurrent-writer negative control in this feature. The host-bound recovery delivery only guards compensation ownership; it does not claim general read-decide-write isolation. Item remains open and unclaimed.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Implementation evidence (feat/write-time-preconditions): one expected-revision precondition enforced inside the locked item store. core/store/item-mutation-precondition.ts gained an AsyncLocalStorage revision scope. assertItemMutationPreconditions compares hashDocument(locked document) with the declared item_hash before any write, and advanceItemMutationPreconditions moves it to the scope's own committed revision. Every mutateItem caller, deleteItem and restore (now also advancing) are therefore guarded without per-command wiring, including bulk update-many rows and extension commands that mutate through the SDK. Public SDK: sdk/lifecycle/item-revision.ts (readItemRevision, withExpectedItemRevisions with a checked/unchecked receipt, parseExpectHashSpecs, isItemRevisionConflict, describeItemRevisionChanges), plus PmClient.readItemRevision/withExpectedItemRevisions. Transports: global --expect-hash <item_hash|id=item_hash> (cli/expected-revisions.ts binds after preAction resolves the tracker root and command <id>), and expectHash on SDK runAction/MCP for 19 item-writing actions. pm get reports item_hash (equal to the latest history after_hash), and stdin-json accepts it as a read-only envelope key so get output still round-trips. The refusal item_revision_conflict (exit 4) carries item_id, expected_revision, current_revision (now rendered in the JSON envelope for every compare-and-set refusal) and details.changes_since, the newest 10 history entries with top-level fields. GH-1620: workspace-transaction docs and JSDoc now state that the lock serializes coordinators only. A negative-control spec shows the peer write is lost without the guard and refused with it. Lexicon budgets grow by exactly one inherited host flag (SHARED_HOST_FLAG_GROWTH) with no spare allowance.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: A precondition scoped with AsyncLocalStorage and evaluated inside the locked item store covers every write path (lifecycle, annotations, links, deps, restore, delete, bulk rows, extension commands) without per-command wiring. The scope's checked/unchecked receipt doubles as a detector for declared-but-unread transport parameters: it caught pm-wsqxwb, where pm_comments/pm_files top-level add silently reads.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Every shared global flag counts toward every command's ratcheted flag-lexicon budget (111 budgets). Adding one host flag means growing all of them by exactly one through SHARED_HOST_FLAG_GROWTH in flag-lexicon-contracts.ts, never by loosening individual ratchets. Global options also leak into update-many's option bag unless invocation-options deletes them.

patch.value: A write based on a stale observed revision refuses atomically and supplies bounded recovery evidence

A revision scope (AsyncLocalStorage) is evaluated in the locked item store after the item lock is taken and before any write, and advances past the scope's own commits. It covers every mutateItem caller, delete, restore, bulk rows and extension SDK writes. Public SDK readItemRevision/withExpectedItemRevisions with a checked/unchecked receipt. Global --expect-hash (bare hash binds <id>, <id>=<hash> names targets). expectHash on 19 MCP/runAction item-writing actions. The refusal carries expected/current revision plus details.changes_since (10 newest history entries with fields). stdin-json accepts item_hash. GH-1620: transaction docs state the lock serializes coordinators only, and a negative-control spec proves the guard turns the lost update into a refusal.

Verified: a stale close/update/comment/files/restore/delete refuses with exit 4 and writes nothing. The fresh revision is admitted, and a multi-write claim+update advances. An interleaved unscoped peer write refuses the next step. update-many fails only the stale row. MCP handleRequest refuses a stale pm_update. 100/100/100/100 coverage and the full quality:static chain pass.

Expected item revisions shipped: pm get reports item_hash, and every locked item write refuses item_revision_conflict when an expected revision no longer holds, across CLI --expect-hash, MCP/runAction expectHash and SDK withExpectedItemRevisions

value.text: Codex review round 1 on PR 1654 (gpt-6.1-sol xhigh): all 8 findings verified and fixed with regression specs. P1 CLI binding used a module-global scope, so overlapping in-process invocations could bind into each other; the binding scope now travels in AsyncLocalStorage, and tokens outside a scope refuse. P1 history-redact/repair/compact bypassed the check; executeHistoryRewrite now asserts under the stream lock and advances after its rewrite. P1 restore of a peer-deleted item matched no expectation because the tombstone has empty metadata; assert/advance take an explicit target id, delete advances to the tombstone revision, and restore is judged under its own id. P2 a supplied but empty --expect-hash value silently dropped the guard; it now refuses with expect_hash_invalid. P2 PmClient revision helpers ran outside extension activation; they now use the client's extension context. P2 stale bulk rows kept only a message; update-many/close-many rows carry error_code, expected_revision and current_revision. P2 plan, test-all and history maintenance were missing from the strict expectHash schema list. Full coverage 100/100/100/100 and full quality:static pass after the fixes.

value.text: Review round 2+3 on PR 1654 (Codex round 2 plus 13 CodeRabbit threads), all verified and fixed with specs. Deleted items bind through retained history, with the delete's tombstone after_hash as their revision. History maintenance of a peer-deleted item is judged as its tombstone. A supplied null expectHash refuses. PmClient binds inside the extension context and runs outside it, so extension commands dispatch. One expect-hash-actions.ts inventory drives both schema and admission (item-reopen admitted). Store call sites pass the locked located.id. When a peer writes during the lock wait, restore and history maintenance return the typed item_revision_conflict instead of generic drift. Unchecked warnings decorate a shallow copy, so frozen results are safe. Stale bulk rows carry details.changes_since. GlobalOptions.expectHash is documented as CLI-scope only.

value.text: Review round 4 on PR 1654 (Codex round 3 plus 4 CodeRabbit threads), all verified and fixed. A guard nested in options (expectHash or expect_hash) is now enforced, via src/sdk/runtime/expect-hash-input.ts, instead of being silently ignored. History rewrites that move the item (legacy Markdown to TOON, or a type folder change) re-locate before advancing. The history context lookup uses the locked located.id.

value.text: Codex review round 4 on PR 1654, all fixed with specs. PmClient revision reads and bindings use a full settings read, so file-backed schema types (schema/types.json) are hydrated and a live custom-type item is no longer misread as its tombstone. Linked-test result recording (test --run, and test-all with tracking enabled) stays best-effort but now propagates a stale declared revision as item_revision_conflict instead of a write_failed warning.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 6 on PR 1654, both fixed with specs. Bindings now store the item's embedded id (read at bind time), and every locked assert/advance matches the entry by either the locked probe id or the embedded id. A write reached through another spelling (a case variant on a case-insensitive filesystem, or a short id) is therefore still guarded. History maintenance gates its extra read on hasActiveItemRevisionScope. An undefined expectHash (top-level or nested) now behaves like an omitted guard: present keys are stripped before dispatch, while arguments with no placement pass through untouched.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 7 on PR 1654, all fixed with specs. The revision-scope store is now one process-wide AsyncLocalStorage registered under Symbol.for('@unbrained/pm-cli/item-revision-scopes'), because the published SDK entrypoints are separate bundle graphs and a guard opened through /sdk must constrain writes made through /sdk/core (specced by loading the module twice). isItemRevisionConflict checks structurally (isPmCliExpectedError plus code), so a refusal from another bundle's PmCliError class is recognized. Delete advances the tombstone expectation through the pre-delete embedded id as an alias, so a delete-then-restore through a case-variant spelling no longer conflicts with itself.

value.text: Codex review round 8 on PR 1654, all fixed with specs. The pre-existing transaction preconditions (validate, committed, historyContext) match either identity of the locked item again (probe spelling or embedded id), restoring upsert_match_changed for case-variant ids. Revision scopes compare trackers by physical path (realpath, only when a scope is active), so a symlinked tracker spelling is guarded. A bare --expect-hash binds to the registered id argument at its actual index (plan add-step <id> works); plan create, whose id slot is a title, needs an explicit target.

value.text: Codex review round 10 on PR 1654, all fixed with specs. A guarded test/test-all --background refuses with expect_hash_background_unsupported, because the worker runs in another process the scope cannot reach. Stripping a guard from runAction options keeps the CLI and literal mutation-input markers and the stdin policy (transferMutationStdinTokenPolicy), so marked inputs like assignee none keep their CLI meaning. Conflict evidence anchors on a before_hash when the matching state's after_hash used another digest (SHA-512), so changes_since is not lost.

value.text: Codex review round 11 on PR 1654, all fixed. The CLI binds expectations to the tracker the command will actually write (resolvePmRoot of the effective global path after extension parser and preflight overrides), so a redirected tracker cannot bypass a guard. A custom field named expect_hash is now routed through the repeatable field option in collision diagnostics, because options.expectHash is consumed as a guard. A bare guard binds to the nested options.id that lifecycle dispatch accepts, with the same precedence.

value.text: Codex review round 12 on PR 1654, both fixed. The CLI guard binds to the post-parser tracker path, because final dispatch rebuilds global options from Commander and reruns only parser overrides; a preflight path change never reaches the writer. validate joins the expect-hash inventory, because --auto-fix and --prune-missing write existing items through audited mutation paths.

value.text:
Codex review round 13 (PR #1654), all fixed in this branch:
1. Extension rewrite seam: final dispatch rebuilds globals from Commander and reruns only parser overrides, while preAction sees parser+preflight output and the injected extension SDK client sees a third view. A guard bound to any single view could check one item while the write lands on another. The fix records the typed invocation (args + path) before overrides, compares the parser and preflight stages with it (invocationRewritten), and refuses a guarded invocation whose tracker or arguments an override rewrote with expect_hash_invocation_rewritten (exit 2). Unrewritten invocations bind to the typed view, which every stage then agrees on.
2. validate --auto-fix / --prune-missing swallowed item_revision_conflict into failed[] and exited 0. The fix: once every fix was attempted, the first typed conflict is re-thrown (throwFirstItemRevisionConflict, exported from sdk/lifecycle/item-revision), so a stale guard exits 4.
3. Gate fallout: validate.ts is held at the 3400-line cap. The rewritten-invocation refusal lives in the SDK module, so cli/expected-revisions no longer imports private core modules (sdk_import_boundary). The error catalog, contracts, agent surfaces (REFUSAL_CLOSURE_CENSUS) and the SDK surface snapshot are regenerated.
Specs: tests/unit/cli/expected-revisions.spec.ts covers both the rewrite detector and the refusal, plus an in-process validate --auto-fix negative control (a peer edit after the read, then exit 4 with item_revision_conflict).

Codex review round 14 (PR #1654), all fixed in this branch:
1. [P1] Final-dispatch parser rewrite: Commander dispatch reruns extension parsers after preAction bound the guard. A parser that returned the typed view on its preAction pass and a different id on its dispatch pass wrote the other item unguarded. Both dispatch-time parser passes (the action wrapper and the dynamic extension command runner) now compare their output with their input via assertGuardedDispatchUnchanged. A guarded invocation whose tracker path or positionals change refuses with expect_hash_invocation_rewritten. A negative control was rebuilt without the check: the redirected update succeeded and wrote the other item.
2. [P2] get --fields item.item_hash: the revision facet shadowed a custom metadata field named item_hash (normalizeAddFieldInput accepts that name). The bare item_hash selects the revision; the item-qualified spelling projects the metadata field again, as at the merge base. A negative control on the old get.ts fails the new spec.
3. [P3] Inventory commands (package/extension inventory) dispatch without lifecycle hooks, so --expect-hash was silently dropped there, malformed values included. The inventory branch now validates the flag, then refuses with expect_hash_requires_mutation (constructor exported as expectHashRequiresMutationError).
Also merged main after the 2026.11.3 release cut and regenerated CHANGELOG.md: the textual merge had placed pm-urzubi under 2026.11.3; it belongs in Unreleased.

Codex review round 15 (PR #1654), all fixed in this branch:
1. [P2] close auto-unblock fan-out: a guarded dependent's item_revision_conflict was caught and turned into an untyped auto_unblock_failed warning, so close reported success. The fan-out now finishes, then refuses with the first dependent's typed conflict. The message discloses that the blocker's close already committed; code, item_id and revisions are preserved, and the CLI still enriches changes_since.
2. [P2] Bulk rollback rows: update-many/close-many --rollback reduced a revision refusal to {id,status,error}. rollbackMutationCheckpoint now captures each item's failure and enriches failed rows with itemRevisionConflictRowFields, the same fields forward rows carry. Both rollback row types now extend ItemRevisionConflictRowFields.
3. [P3] Revision scope entries now track committed explicitly, set by advanceItemMutationPreconditions. Previously "Earlier writes already committed" was inferred from expected != declared, which a restore-then-delete cycle (back to the declared tombstone) falsified.
Negative controls: all three new item-revision.spec.ts cases fail on the prior source.

Codex review round 16 (PR #1654), all fixed in this branch:
1. [P2] Guarded restore over an unreadable live file: readRestoreItem reconstructs the document from history, so the guard judged the reconstruction, not the corrupt live bytes, and restore overwrote them while reporting the expectation as checked. assertItemRevisionExpectationsOnUnreadable (core/store/item-mutation-precondition) now refuses a bound expectation when the live document required recovery: current_revision is the SHA-256 of the unreadable text, and required names an unguarded pm restore. Unguarded restore recovery is unchanged.
2. [P2] close-many after the round-15 fan-out refusal: the committed close was counted as a failed row (closed_count 0, outcome dependency_failed), with the dependent's revision fields filed under the blocker's id. The refusal now discloses the committed close as side_effects [{path: history/<id>.jsonl, op: close}]. close-many reports that row as closed, with warning auto_unblock_refused:<dependent>:item_revision_conflict and the dependent's typed fields under dependent_revision_conflict.
3. [P3] deps is a conditional mutation in the history-scope inventory but only reads, so --expect-hash on it now refuses with expect_hash_requires_mutation.
Negative controls: each new spec fails on the prior source.

value.text: Codex review round 17 (PR #1654), fixed: (1) [P2] A final-dispatch extension parser could add background: true to a guarded test-all after preAction admitted it in the foreground; the worker never evaluates the guard. assertGuardedDispatchUnchanged now also re-runs assertExpectHashAdmissible on each dispatch pass's options, so a late --background refuses with expect_hash_background_unsupported. (2) [P2] update-many --status closed routes through close, so the committed-close misreport fixed for close-many in round 16 also hit update-many rows. Both bulk commands now share committedCloseDependentConflict (sdk/lifecycle/close): it reads the refusal's side_effects close disclosure, and the row reports as updated/closed with auto_unblock_refused and dependent_revision_conflict. A negative control on the prior update-many.ts fails the new spec.

value.text: Codex review round 18 (PR #1654), fixed: (1) [P2] history-repair --salvage-tail bypassed the revision guard: salvageHistoryTail rewrites history outside executeHistoryRewrite. Under the salvage lock it now judges the live item revision (assertItemRevisionExpectationsOnUnreadable for an unreadable live file, the tombstone with no live file), then advances after the write. (2) [P2] Bulk history-compact --ids and history-repair --all rows reduced item_revision_conflict to an error string; both row types now extend ItemRevisionConflictRowFields. The SDK surface acknowledges the two optional-field widenings. Before this round I swept every guarded action's catch blocks for error flattening: annotations/comments/structured-mutations only parse input, task-composition keeps the typed context, and no other guarded path drops the conflict. Negative controls fail both new specs on the prior source.

value.text: Codex review round 19 (PR #1654), fixed: (1) [P2] A file whose embedded id names another item (tasks/pm-a.toon containing id: pm-b) bound its expectation only to pm-b. After an unscoped identity repair, both locked-store identities were pm-a, so a stale guarded update matched nothing and succeeded. Binding and readItemRevision now refuse such a file with item_identity_conflict until the identity is repaired; case-only differences still bind. (2) [P2] Tail salvage's lock-wait drift check threw the generic retry refusal before the revision assertion, so a guard the peer's edit made stale got no typed fields. The drift path now judges a fresh under-lock item snapshot first. Also restored the round-15 auto-unblock catch to one c8-ignore region: the full coverage run of 0b4c04e64 found its new non-conflict branch uncovered. Negative controls fail both new specs on the prior source.

value.text: Codex review round 20 (PR #1654), fixed: (1) [P2] The round-19 identity check case-folded both ids, so on a case-sensitive filesystem pm-a.toon embedding PM-A still bound under PM-A, and a peer's case repair could detach the guard. Binding now compares the embedded id with the physical file spelling via resolvePhysicalItemId, shared with blocker resolution (sdk/query/declared-blockers), so both apply one identity rule; case-insensitive probe aliases still bind. (2) [P2] My round-19 salvage drift read re-opened the obsolete subject.located path: an item a peer moved or deleted during the lock wait threw ENOENT even for unguarded salvage. It now reads the fresh under-lock location. Negative controls fail both new specs on the prior source. Process note: the gate run of f71056b92 hit two deps-command 30 s timeouts because Codex ran concurrently; the spec passes alone (41/41), so gates now run without a concurrent review.

value.text: Codex review round 21 (PR #1654), fixed: (1) [P2] Change evidence is now best-effort: a malformed history entry (a null line, which readHistoryEntries accepts) made describeItemRevisionChanges throw a TypeError during enrichment, replacing item_revision_conflict. enrichItemRevisionConflict now returns the original typed refusal when evidence cannot be built. (2) [P2] The close fan-out refusal's side_effects named only the close, so a dependent already unblocked before the refused one lost its committed-write evidence. side_effects now lists the close and each unblocked dependent (op update), and bulk rows add auto_unblocked:<id> warnings from them. (3) [P2] assertExpectHashAdmissible classifies space-separated CLI subcommand paths as their native action (package catalog -> package-catalog), so CLI and SDK refuse the same read commands. Negative controls fail all three new cases on the prior source.

value.text: Codex review round 22 (PR #1654): the one finding (P2) is filed as pm-thbdxu, not fixed here. An item_store_write override that transforms contents makes the scope advance to the pre-override hash, so a guarded scope's own second write falsely conflicts. That direction fails closed (a false refusal, never a lost update). The review loop applied the convergence rule after 21 fixed rounds: each later round found narrower states in code the previous round had just hardened. Anything below P1 is now tracked as a follow-up with its own acceptance criteria.
